memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "When that year was over, they came to him the following year and said, 'We cannot hide from our lord the fact that since our money is gone and our livestock belongs to you, there is nothing left for our lord except our bodies and our land. Why should we perish before your eyes—we and our land as well? Buy us and our land in exchange for food, and we with our land will be in bondage to Pharaoh. Give us seed so that we may live and not die, and that the land may not become desolate.'" — Gen 47:18-19 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
"There is nothing left except our bodies and our land." The famine has taken everything else. And so they offer the last thing they have — themselves.

It is a desperate proposal, and they are the ones who make it. They would rather be alive in bondage than free and dead.

There is something in this that reaches into our own experience. Human beings will sell themselves to almost anything that promises to keep them alive. We hand ourselves over to work, to approval, to substances, to relationships, to whatever seems to hold us up — and we call it necessity.

Scripture is blunt about this. Everyone serves something. Jesus said we cannot serve two masters (Matt 6:24), and Paul wrote that we are slaves to whatever we obey (Rom 6:16). The question was never whether we would belong to something. It is what.

The gospel is not that we become independent. It is that we are bought by a good Master. We were bought at a price (1 Cor 6:20) — not with silver or gold, but with the precious blood of Christ (1 Pet 1:18-19). And His service, unlike Egypt's, is called freedom.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What have you handed yourself over to in order to feel secure?
2. Is there a difference between how you serve God and how you serve other things?
3. What does it mean to you that you were bought at a price?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, I have given myself to things that cannot hold me. Thank You that You bought me with Your own blood and that serving You is true freedom. Amen.
